title: mesh_boolean output has unwelded duplicate vertices
description:
skull.dsl produces a mesh with 22107 vertices and only 7369 faces after three mesh_boolean operations. Welded triangle meshes satisfy V ≈ F/2 + 2, so for 7369 faces expected vertex count is ~3687. We're at 22107 — 6x more. Each boolean split adds new cut-line vertices without welding against existing coincident vertices, and the result cascades.

Impact observed in VIEW-7: SemanticPatchDecomposer running on the ArrayMesh-converted boolean output produces ONE patch per face (7369 patches for 7369 faces) because the duplicate vertices make every face topologically isolated — shared edges between adjacent faces use different vertex ids on each side, so face-face adjacency lookup finds no neighbour.

Current workaround: users append merge_by_distance(0.0001) after the last boolean in their DSL. We can see this happening in coons-cage DSLs. mesh_boolean should do this weld itself, or at minimum offer a 'weld_output: bool' parameter defaulting to true.

This is surfaced by MESH-49 (node canonicalization) but is a distinct correctness issue: even if we canonicalize to ArrayMesh, mesh_boolean's output is topologically wrong.

Related: MESH-49 canonicalization plan. PATCH epic's ability to decompose DSL-generated meshes is blocked until this is fixed.
definition-of-done: mesh_boolean welds coincident vertices before returning (threshold configurable, default 1e-4). Verified on skull.dsl: vertex count drops to roughly F/2 + 2, and SemanticPatchDecomposer produces a reasonable patch count (~100\u2013300 not 7369).
testing-plan: 1. Load skull.dsl in mesh viewer. Check log: verts should be ~3700 not 22107. 2. Press P: decomposition should produce \u2264 500 patches. 3. Render visually to confirm no gaps or flipped normals from the weld.
